headline: Saudi employees limited to five contracts a year for Nitaqat counting
summary: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Human Resources has introduced updated rules for its Nitaqat Saudization program, stipulating that Saudi employees will only count toward quotas if they have five or fewer registered contracts over a 52-week period. Under the new Qiwa platform regulations, workers are limited to two concurrent jobs and capped at seven total contracts within a 365-day window. Furthermore, to qualify for Nitaqat counting, employees must be full-time non-students earning a minimum monthly salary of SR4,000.

headline: Case-in-Point: The employee who doesn’t want to become a manager
summary: Meera Pillai, a top-performing software engineer at Meridian Software, has repeatedly declined promotions into management to remain focused on technical specialization. Her decision forces HR to reconsider traditional career ladders and evaluate how to offer growth, influence, and fair compensation to elite individual contributors. The case highlights the organizational challenge of valuing high-level technical expertise without forcing specialists into people-management roles.

headline: JPMorgan names Mark O’Donovan as new HR head
summary: JPMorgan Chase has appointed 30-year company veteran Mark O’Donovan as its next head of human resources, effective January 2027. Currently serving as CEO of international consumer banking, O’Donovan will succeed retiring HR chief Robin Leopold and join the bank's operating committee. The planned transition underscores a growing trend in global finance to blend deep operational leadership with workforce and technology strategy.

headline: Vishal Upadhyay moves up the HR leadership ranks at Waree Group
summary: Waree Group has promoted Vishal Upadhyay to Vice President of Human Resources after a 12-year tenure with the Indian renewable energy company. Throughout his career at Waree, Upadhyay has driven key HR initiatives across solar and lithium-ion manufacturing sectors, including digital transformation and workforce optimization. His promotion reflects the company's focus on strengthening its people leadership as it continues to expand in the renewable energy market.

headline: HCLTech offers Rs 18 lakh starting salary as it steps up ‘Elite Engineer’ hiring
summary: HCLTech is adopting a skills-based hiring model for its upcoming intake of roughly 11,000 freshers, with starting salaries ranging from Rs 4.5 lakh to Rs 18 lakh. The top pay tier is dedicated to an expanded 'Elite Engineer' cadre from premier institutes targeting frontier tech roles such as AI, quantum, and semiconductors. This widening salary gap highlights how IT firms are placing higher monetary value on specialized technical skills over standard degrees.

headline: PhonePe marks 10 years by trying to name all 70 crore users
summary: To mark its 10-year anniversary and celebrate reaching 70 crore registered users, PhonePe has launched a consumer-focused brand campaign created in partnership with Ogilvy. The anthem film features India's fastest speaker attempting to name every user, illustrating that even at record speed, the task would take 980 consecutive days. The campaign aims to shift the narrative from a standard corporate milestone to a tribute thanking individual consumers for driving India's digital growth.
